newsitem.title: UK: Emerging debt dealers await Brazil Brady buy-back. [CORRECTED 14:32 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt dealers await Brazil Brady buy-back. [CORRECTED 14:32 GMT]

text.p: A subdued Brady market turned its attention to Tuesday's launch of Brazil's expected $1.0 billion 30-year global bond as part of a Brady buy-back, emerging market debt dealers said on Monday.
They said the deal would have a positive impact on the market as a whole and spreads should tighten.
Brazil will swap (corrects to read "swap" instead of "buy back") its "C" bonds BR8D14=RR, Discs BRFLTD24=RR and Par BR4D24=RR bonds or swap these Brady instruments for a new 30-year global bond.
Part of the new global bond can also be bought outright for cash.
"The key ingredient for Bradies today is the Brazil deal tomorrow," BankAmerica emerging markets economist Richard Gray said.
"Immediately after the Brady swap, spreads will tighten which will give a lift to Brazilian bonds and the market in general," he added.
The $1.0 billion global bond is being issued as part of a Brazilian effort to swap or buy back Brady bonds. The offer will expire June 3 unless extended by Brazil.
Price talk now among dealers and investors pegged the global at about 375 to 385 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Investor presentations have been held in London, New York and Boston.
Brazil's bonds were firm, all up 1/8, they said.
Brazilian Pars BR4D24=RR were 1/8 up, bid at 66-1/8, Discs BRFLTD24=RR were also 1/8 up bid at 83 and Cs BR8D14=RR were 1/8 up bid at 79-3/8.
Brazil's Cs were seen the least attractive swap option because unlike Pars and Discs, they are uncollateralized and an exchange would not be as lucrative to investors.
